note: Canonical proof-interchange wrapper for DerivationWireV1. Each binding builds the named fixture from contract DTO constructors, encodes Tuple[Atom(wrapper_tag), DerivationWirePayloadV1], and must reproduce wire_hex. Positive fixtures cover leaf, builtin, rule+positive premise, and the trailing optional closed_world certificate slot through a Count premise. Malformed fixtures are authored as raw wrapper bytes and must reject. #2630 (seat:caa's ruling): every malformed row carries `refusal`, the EXACT text the one decoder gives in all three cores (`decode <path>: <defect>`), and `layer`: `wrapper` rows are refused by the contract's full-wire decoder, `payload` rows also by the kernel seam handed the unwrapped payload. `decodes` rows must be ACCEPTED and re-encode byte for byte (a root that indexes no node passes to check; a subst in canonical order). The refusal rows and texts are stated by scripts/vectors/derivation_wire_refusal_oracle.py, from the spec, calibrated against this file's own rows (`--check` verifies them).

positive.name: closed_world_count_partial
positive.note: ADR 0030 D4 - LANDED (checker version 3): a cert with BOTH trailing-optional elements, the D10 slice-seal witness digest (d1 x 32) at the 11th slot and `partial_scope` = StratumPrefix {level 1, [sealed]} at the 12th. Same bytes as the RED-first `malformed` entry of b1d3d5a7, which every pre-0030 decoder refused by arity - so the flip is the decoder, not the fixture. A wire round-trip fixture: the level-1 partial scope over a level-0 seal is deliberately NOT a checkable cert (check() refuses `cert_partial_scope_invalid` on the level mismatch); what is pinned here is the ENCODING. Built by each binding from its DTO constructors as `closed_world_count_partial`.

malformed.name: cert_domain_values_not_canonical
malformed.note: issue #839: a closed_world cert whose finite-domain values arrive on the wire OUT of canonical sorted+deduped codec-byte order (b before a). The wire encoding PROMISES canonical order; the decoder must CHECK it, not assume it (rs/go previously admitted the bytes verbatim, silently defeating binary-search membership downstream) and not repair it (ts previously re-sorted, masking the producer bug and diverging from rs/go on identical bytes). Decode must REJECT.

malformed.refusal: decode closed_world.cert.domain.values: not in canonical sorted+deduped order

malformed.name: cert_domain_values_duplicated
malformed.note: issue #2545: the finite domain's value `a` twice, in canonical order but NOT deduped. The duplicated sibling of cert_domain_values_not_canonical, minted from it by the ontos codec with only that collection changed. The contract decoders refuse it (#839), and so must all three kernel seam decoders, with seam_refusal: a host that kept it verbatim or deduplicated it would decode one guest frame into different certificates.

malformed.name: adr0030_cert_thirteen_elements_closed_posture
malformed.note: ADR 0030 D4 - the closed posture, re-pinned one element further out: the `closed_world_count_partial` cert with a THIRTEENTH element (an Atom of one byte, x) appended. A decoder that knows the twelve-element form must still refuse an arity it does not know, exactly as every pre-0030 decoder refused twelve; defaulting an unknown trailing element would WIDEN what a certificate can claim. Derived from the twelve-element bytes by the same codec walker, one element appended.

decodes.name: root_out_of_range_decodes
decodes.note: #2630, `seat:caa`'s ruling on #2645: the `leaf` fixture with its root set to 1 over its one node. The decoder ACCEPTS it and preserves the root, because a Derivation can hold it and check refuses it by its FIRM root_out_of_range (#2650 keeps the planner from reading it first).

decodes.name: subst_in_canonical_order_decodes
decodes.note: #2630: the control for `subst_duplicate_var` and `subst_misordered`, with X before Y in codec(key) order. It decodes and re-encodes byte for byte.

decodes.name: subst_bom_prefixed_var_is_a_distinct_var_decodes
decodes.note: #2682: the `rule` fixture's subst with var X and var BOM+X, in codec(key) order (the shorter atom first). A var-id is its exact bytes, so these are TWO variables and the subst re-encodes with both. ts's default TextDecoder stripped the BOM, keyed both as X and silently kept ONE value; rs and go always kept both.

decodes.name: subst_term_quoted_var_utf8_decodes
decodes.note: #3102: the control for subst_term_quoted_var_not_utf8, the same entry with its quoted variable named é (c3 a9, the same lead byte as a two-byte ill-formed name). A subst term is any quoted term, so it decodes and re-encodes byte for byte.

decodes.name: root_at_index_max_decodes
decodes.note: #2682 ruling A: the `leaf` fixture's root at INDEX_MAX = 2^53 - 1, the largest in-domain index. Every core decodes it; check refuses it as root_out_of_range (vectors/check.json root_at_index_max_out_of_range). One past it is the malformed row root_past_index_max.

decodes.name: root_past_32_bit_offset_decodes
decodes.note: #2735 (seat:caa, correcting #2682's ruling A): the `leaf` fixture's root at 2^32 + 5, in the contract's domain and past what a 32-bit usize/int holds. Every core decodes it as the integer it is, on every build (the per-platform IndexBeyondPlatform refusal is deleted), and check refuses it as root_out_of_range (vectors/check.json root_past_32_bit_offset_out_of_range).

decodes.name: limits_decl_at_index_max_decodes
decodes.note: #2682 ruling A: the `closed_world_count` certificate's limits_decl.cert_facts at INDEX_MAX. A caller-configurable work budget may be this large, so the interface is not narrowed to a 32-bit width (ADR 0012). One past it is limits_decl_past_index_max.

decodes.name: count_arity_at_u32_max_decodes
decodes.note: #2682: the `closed_world_count` count premise's pred arity at 2^32 - 1, the largest u32. One past it is count_arity_past_u32.

decodes.name: scope_level_at_u32_max_decodes
decodes.note: #2682: the `closed_world_count` certificate's scope level at 2^32 - 1. One past it is scope_level_past_u32.

decodes.name: support_rank_at_u32_max_decodes
decodes.note: research 0028 A18 (#3024): `closed_world_count` given one support edge at rank 2^32 - 1, the largest u32. One past it is support_rank_past_u32.

decodes.name: support_ref_rank_at_u32_max_decodes
decodes.note: research 0028 A18 (#3024): the same edge with one same_stratum body ref at rank 2^32 - 1. One past it is support_ref_rank_past_u32.

decodes.name: ground_arg_256_term_levels_decodes
decodes.note: #2731 (`seat:caa`'s ruling): the `leaf` fixture with its first argument s(s(...s(z)...)) 256 TERM levels deep, 512 value levels once quoted: exactly check's default max_term_depth. It decodes in every core, and check.json's `term_depth_256_at_the_default_accept` checks the same conclusion. rs's decoder refused it `TooDeep` (a fixed 256-VALUE-level guard, about 128 term levels) until #2731, while go and ts decoded it: the spec's tri-core promise was false at the defaults.

decodes.name: ground_arg_257_term_levels_decodes
decodes.note: #2731: the same at 257 term levels, one past check's default. It still DECODES in every core: the decoder has no depth policy, and the refusal belongs to check alone (check.json's `term_depth_257_past_the_default_term_too_deep`, code term_too_deep).
